fields.name: Conversation
fields.note: What people actually say to one another — the everyday words that carry tone as much as meaning.

fields.name: Stories & Fiction
fields.note: The register of novels: how a scene is set, how a character is drawn, how a moment is held.

fields.name: News & Opinion
fields.note: How events are reported and argued over — the vocabulary of headlines, columns and comment.

fields.name: Character & Feeling
fields.note: What someone is like and what they are feeling: temperament, mood and motive.

fields.name: Things & Places
fields.note: The physical world — objects, materials, weather, rooms and landscapes.

fields.name: Time & Change
fields.note: How things begin, continue, falter and end.

words.d: Saying what you think directly, without softening it.
words.e: She was *blunt* about the delay: nobody would be paid this month.
words.n: Not rude in itself, but close to it. "Blunt" excuses the speaker; "rude" does not.

words.d: Uncomfortable, or causing discomfort — of a person, a silence or a situation.
words.e: There was an *awkward* pause before anyone answered.
words.a: مُحرِج — أو أخرق إذا وُصِف به شخص

words.d: Unnecessary excitement or complaint about something small.
words.e: He made a terrible *fuss* about a ten-minute wait.

words.d: Thin and hollow-looking, usually from illness, hunger or long strain.
words.e: A *gaunt* figure stood in the doorway, thinner than when she last saw him.
words.a: نحيل شاحب — هزيل من مرض أو جوع

words.d: To stay longer than expected, or to be slow to fade.
words.e: The smell of smoke *lingered* in the hall for days.
words.a: يتلكّأ — يبقى أطول من المتوقَّع، أو يظلّ أثره

words.d: The darker part of twilight, after sunset and before night.
words.e: They reached the river at *dusk*, with just enough light to cross.

words.d: To state something as fact without having proved it.
words.e: The report *alleges* that the money was moved before the audit.
words.n: Carries doubt on purpose. Writing "alleges" where you mean "says" quietly accuses someone.

words.d: A strong, hostile reaction against a decision or a change.
words.e: The new fee drew an immediate *backlash* from readers.

words.d: To limit something that is growing or getting out of hand.
words.e: The rules are meant to *curb* spending, not to stop it.

words.d: Able to recover quickly from difficulty.
words.e: Children are more *resilient* than the people worrying about them.

words.d: Cautious because you suspect something may go wrong.
words.e: He was *wary* of any offer that arrived unasked.

words.d: Pleased with yourself in a way that annoys other people.
words.e: She gave a *smug* little smile when the figures proved her right.
words.n: Always disapproving. You can never call yourself smug and mean it kindly.

words.d: Too small for what it has to hold.
words.e: Four of them shared one *cramped* room above the shop.

words.d: To spread out widely and without order.
words.e: The city *sprawls* for miles along the coast.
The change was *gradual* enough that nobody marked the day it began.
The meeting came to an *abrupt* end when the line went dead.
words.n: Of a person it means curt, not quick — an "abrupt reply" is a short, cold one.

words.d: A small, round, peppery root vegetable, usually red-skinned and white inside.
words.e: She pulled a handful of *radishes* from the garden and rinsed them for the salad.

words.d: A small gnawing mammal — rats, mice, squirrels.
words.e: The barn was overrun with *rodents* that chewed through the grain sacks.

words.d: A thick hot cereal made by boiling grain, usually oats, in water or milk.
words.e: The prisoners received nothing but thin *porridge* and stale bread.
